texts.facts: Present Appeal has been preferred u/s.29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred as PWDV Act) challenging the order dated 14.02.2024 whereby the trial court has directed Mohit Arora (hereinafter VIRENDER KUMAR referred as respondent) to pay Rs.5000/- per month to the BANSAL complainant Smt. Bindiya Kandhari (hereinafter referred as complainant/appellant) towards maintenance of the daughter by VIRENDER from the date of filing of the petition till she attains the majority 15:10:41 +0530 and has not awarded any maintenance so far as the complainant/appellant is concerned. 2. The brief facts giving rise to the present appeal are that the complainant/appellant got married with the respondent on 04.05.2001 as per Hindu rites and customs. Out of the wedlock, one female child namely Kalindi Arora was born on 21.03.2002. It is alleged that the appellant and the respondent are living separately since 07.10.2014. The appellant has filed the petition under the provisions of PWDV Act. An application for interim maintenance was also moved, which was allowed and the court passed the order of maintenance as mentioned above. Aggrieved by the order, Bindiya Kandhari @ Bindiya Arora vs Mohit Arora on 19 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55385217/ 1 the present appeal has been preferred. 3. Notice of appeal was sent to the respondent. Trial court record was also requisitioned.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the complainant/appellant submitted that the trial court has not exercised its judicial discretion judiciously resulting into miscarriage and failure of justice. The mother has to not only take care of the child and spend money on her upbringing but also has to spend substantial time and make efforts and, therefore, the quantum of maintenance should have been decided accordingly. 6. The daughter of the complainant/appellant is still pursuing her studies and is unable to maintain herself. The child has to be taken care till she is able to maintain herself and not on attaining the majority. Obligation of the respondent herein is to maintain his unmarried daughter till she is able to maintain herself out of her own earnings till she gets the employment. Even the complainant/ appellant has now lost the job in August 2021 regarding which she has already filed the document but the Ld. Trial Court has not considered this fact. She has made lots of efforts but she is not getting any job but the trial court has failed to appreciate this fact and also that respondent is living a lavish life. He has concealed his financial status though the trial court has mentioned this fact but still has not awarded the maintenance as required. 7. The daughter of the complainant/appellant has specific and essential financial needs, encompassing education, healthcare and basic necessities and it is the duty and responsibility of the respondent to fulfill the same. The trial court has totally failed to consider and appreciate the material facts. It is prayed that the maintenance awarded be enhanced and instead of restricting it to the date of attaining of majority, it be till she gets married and the appellant be also awarded maintenance from August 2021 since when she is not employed. 8. A father has a duty and an obligation to maintain his daughters and to take care of their expenses, including towards their education and marriage. Kanya Daan is a solemn and pious obligation of a Hindu Father, from which he cannot renege. This view is clearly not supported by the precedents taken note of hereinabove." 15. The context of Section 125 Cr.P.C., 1973 is to ensure that the wife and the children of the husband are not left in a state of destitution after the divorce. The husband must also carry the financial burden of making certain that his children are capable of attaining a position in society wherein they can sufficiently maintain themselves. The mother cannot be burdened with the entire expenditure on the education of her son just because he has completed 18 years of age, and the father cannot be absolved of all responsibilities to meet the education expenses of his son because the son may have attained the age of majority, but may not be financially independent and could be incapable of sustaining himself. A father is bound to compensate the wife who, after spending on children, may hardly be left with anything to maintain herself." 16. " 11. The marriage between the parties is not in dispute. An order for maintenance pendente lite or for costs of the proceedings is conditional on the circumstance that the wife or husband who makes a claim for the same has no independent income sufficient for her or his support or to meet the necessary expenses of the proceeding. Likewise, the financial position of the wife's parents is also immaterial. The Court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay maintenance and whether the applicant has any independent income sufficient for her or his support.
